title: Completely Mixed Nash Is Subgame Perfect
body_html:
Completely Mixed Nash Is Subgame Perfect

Let $\Gamma$ be an extensive-form game. Every Nash equilibrium in completely mixed strategies, whether behavior strategies or mixed strategies in the textbook statement, is a subgame-perfect equilibrium.

Lean Scope

The legacy Arena theorem ExtensiveGame.IsBehaviorNashEq.toSubgamePerfect_of_isCompletelyMixed remains an interface-form behavior-strategy statement: it packages positive reach as ExtensiveGame.BehaviorProfile.IsCompletelyMixedWithPositiveReach and uses ExtensiveGame.ReachedSubgamePayoffTransfer.

The finite imperfect-information layer now contains a stronger behavior- strategy formalization: FiniteImperfectGame.IsBehaviorNashEqWithChance.toSubgamePerfect_of_isCompletelyMixed_finiteHorizon. It works with information-set-indexed behavior strategies, explicit full-support chance probabilities, legal reachable subgames, and finite outside/continuation horizon hypotheses. In that theorem, positive reach of each legal subgame root is derived from complete mixing by FiniteImperfectGame.behaviorReachProbFromWithChance_pos_of_before_reachable; the payoff decomposition is derived by the existing finite-horizon Theorem 7.5 lemma FiniteImperfectGame.IsBehaviorNashEqWithChance.restrictReachableSubgame_of_reachProb_pos_finiteHorizon.

The full textbook statement also covers mixed strategies. The finite imperfect-information layer now records the mixed complete-mixing predicates, proves that a completely mixed independent mixed profile assigns positive product probability to every pure-strategy profile, and provides the simplex conditioning primitive used by reached-subgame mixed continuations. It also defines FiniteImperfectGame.MixedProfile.conditionedRestrictReachableSubgame, which first conditions each player's mixed strategy on compatibility with the unique pre-root path and then restricts pure strategies to the reachable subgame. The positive-reach side has also been pushed into the mixed layer: FiniteImperfectGame.MixedProfile.IsCompletelyMixed.reachProbFromWithChance_pos_textbook derives strictly positive mixed reach probability from complete mixing, full-support chance, and the textbook finite-tree outside horizon. For the factorization side, the module now names the player-local event product and chance-path product as FiniteImperfectGame.MixedProfile.textbookReachFactor, proves that it is strictly positive under complete mixing and full-support chance, and proves FiniteImperfectGame.MixedProfile.reachProbFromWithChance_eq_textbookReachFactor: the recursive mixed reach probability at the textbook outside horizon equals the product of the player-local path event and the chance path product. The player-local part is factored through FiniteImperfectGame.mixedProfileProductEventProb_eq_prod_eventProb and FiniteImperfectGame.MixedProfile.textbookPathEventProb_eq_productEventProb. The module also records that FiniteImperfectGame.MixedProfile.IsCompletelyMixed.textbookContinuation is an independent player-wise mixed profile rather than a correlated continuation object.

This is the intended textbook continuation object for the mixed version of Corollary 7.7, and FiniteImperfectGame.IsTextbookMixedSubgamePerfectWithChance records the final target shape without exposing a user-supplied finite-fuel parameter or a behavior-strategy conclusion. The mixed Theorem 7.5 cancellation step is now available as FiniteImperfectGame.IsMixedNashEqWithChance.restrictReachableSubgame_of_reachProb_pos. Its type no longer takes the older mixed payoff-transfer interface; instead it calls concrete decomposition theorems derived from the recursive mixed semantics: FiniteImperfectGame.TextbookFiniteTree.mixedPayoff_eq_reach_mul_conditioned_add_outside_path for the baseline profile and FiniteImperfectGame.TextbookFiniteTree.mixedSplicePayoff_eq_reach_mul_conditioned_deviate_add_outside_path for the spliced subgame deviation. Using that theorem, the module also proves the mixed Corollary 7.7 wrapper FiniteImperfectGame.IsMixedNashEqWithChance.toSubgamePerfect_of_isCompletelyMixed. Its statement uses FiniteImperfectGame.IsTextbookMixedNashEqWithChance at the original root, complete mixing, full-support chance, and the textbook finite tree; its conclusion is FiniteImperfectGame.IsTextbookMixedSubgamePerfectWithChance.

References

  • [MSZ, Cor. 7.7] Maschler, Solan, and Zamir, Game Theory. A completely mixed Nash equilibrium is subgame-perfect.
